title: Prediction Markets as Macro Derivatives: A Simulation Framework for Portfolio Hedging with Event Contracts
abstract: First empirical framework for evaluating institutional viability of event contract hedging. Models 383 Kalshi contracts across 58 macro events (Fed rate + CPI, 2022–2024) as binary derivatives using modified Black-Scholes on VIX surface. At 1% NAV: hedged Sharpe 0.538 vs unhedged 0.065. Quantifies basis risk (100% CPI accuracy, 0% FOMC, which is itself a market-efficiency finding), hedge efficiency decay, and AUM ceiling ($148K current → $14.8M at 100× ADV). JEL: G11, G13, G14, G18.
author: Kalra, S.

title: PIE: Physics-Inspired Contrastive Learning for Low-Light Image Enhancement
abstract: Bag-of-Curves negative sample generation (gamma, sigmoid, logarithmic curves), contrastive learning with Gram matrix triplet loss + InfoNCE objective, unsupervised superpixel segmentation for regional brightness consistency. Evaluated on LOL dataset and real-world smartphone images. Outperforms RetinexNet (20.7 PSNR), Zero-DCE (21.5), EnlightenGAN (20.9). PIE achieves 24.3 PSNR, 0.89 SSIM.
author: Kalra, S.

title: Bitcoin Volatility and Regime Forecasting: A Comparative Analysis of Time Series Models
abstract: Comparative analysis of OLS, ARIMA, GARCH(1,1) on Bitcoin returns. Confirms Weak-Form EMH, 50% directional accuracy for OLS/ARIMA. GARCH(1,1): α=0.089, β=0.895, persistence=0.984. Crisis simulation across COVID-19 crash, Terra/Luna collapse, FTX bankruptcy, 2021 bull run. Bull/Bear regime classification showing asymmetric duration and 2–3× volatility differential.
author: Kalra, S.

title: PACER: Pressure-Adaptive Continuous Epoch Reclamation
abstract: Tests whether epoch-based reclamation for lock-free data structures can adapt its freeing policy to workload pressure, extending token4 (Kim et al., PPoPP 2024). Implemented in C++ (setbench) and Rust (loom model-checked). The initial 10–22% speedup traced to a use-after-free in the reclaimer; after the fix, PACER ties token4 (0.93–1.03×) on write-only, 80%-read and range-query workloads. A free-count sweep shows why there's no headroom on single-socket hardware. Multi-socket behaviour remains untested.
author: Kalra, S.
